_comment: Registration for the --commands mode of scripts/check-claude-md-budget.py (issue #1669).
WHY A SEPARATE CONTROL from controls/claude-md-budget: a control carries ONE invocation, and
this mode reads a different population (every document under .claude/commands) against a
different budget source (.claude/command-word-budgets.tsv, not the script's DOCUMENT_BUDGETS).
Blinding one mode does not blind the other.
WHY THIS GATE NEEDS ONE: it lets work THROUGH - a prerequisite of `make verify` - and nothing
downstream re-derives it. A blind version prints the same 'ok - N command documents' line over
a command document that has doubled, which is the growth #1669 measured (flow/auto.md 10,183
The cases carry their own budget table, so they do not move when a real budget is lowered.
limits: Covers the WORD COUNT of a declared command document against its declared budget. It does not cover the undeclared-document, stale-entry, malformed-table or empty-population refusals, which report a different line and are pinned by tests/test_check_claude_md_budget.py. It says nothing about whether any real budget is the RIGHT number, nor about whether a trimmed document kept its steps - that is check-claude-md-behavior.py's command-step fixture.

cases.name: bad-command-over-budget
cases.why: flow/example.md at 101 words against a declared budget of 100 - ONE word over, the #1669 acceptance case. Distinct tokens, so it cannot pass for a reason peculiar to the counter.

cases.name: good-command-at-budget
cases.why: The same document at exactly 100 words. Separates a working gate from one wedged at 'fail', and pins the boundary as inclusive.

anchors.why: CONSTRUCTED: the plausible weaker check - every command document has a line in the budget table - with the word count never taken. 'It has a declared budget' mistaken for 'it is inside its declared budget'. It catches an undeclared document and is blind to a declared one over budget: it MISSES the known-bad input and AGREES with the gate on the known-good one.
